extracted.intended_audience: Principal investigators and institutional grant administrators preparing NIH/PHS 398 grant applications (institutional capacity-building/training grants)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and justifying an NIH PHS 398-format institutional grant application and budget (training/capacity-building for grants management), including required cover page supplement sections, budget forms, specific aims, research strategy, and budget justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Research Plan required sections
rubrics_metrics.description: The Research Plan must include: Introduction (for Resubmission/Revision), Specific Aims, Research Strategy, Progress Report Publication List, and other Research Plan sections (Vertebrate Animals, Select Agent Research, Multiple PD/PI Leadership Plan), Consortium/Contractual Arrangements, Letters of Support, Resource Sharing Plan(s), Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources, and Appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Files are attached/named (e.g., Specific_Aims.pdf, Research_Strategy.pdf). Follow PHS 398 ordering and include each listed component where applicable; include the Introduction only for resubmission/revision applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover Page Supplement — Vertebrate Animals section
rubrics_metrics.description: If vertebrate animals are used, indicate whether animals are euthanized and whether the method is consistent with AVMA guidelines; if not consistent, describe method and provide scientific justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer Yes/No to euthanasia and AVMA consistency; provide explanation and justification where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover Page Supplement — Program Income section
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether program income is anticipated during the grant period; if yes, list anticipated amounts and sources by budget period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide Budget Period, Anticipated Amount ($), and Source(s) in the specified format; leave blank if 'No'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover Page Supplement — Human Embryonic Stem Cells section
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the project involves human embryonic stem cells; if yes, list the registry number(s) for specific cell lines or indicate that a registry line will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NIH stem cell registry (link provided) to cite line numbers; check box if specific line cannot be referenced yet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover Page Supplement — Inventions and Patents (Renewals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare whether there are inventions and patents; if yes, indicate whether previously reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer Yes/No and provide follow-up responses as requested on the form for renewal applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover Page Supplement — Change of Investigator/Institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details when there is a change of PD/PI or change of grantee institution, including name of former PD/PI and former institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete identifying fields (prefix, first/middle/last name, suffix) and former institution information when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior/Key Personnel budget completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget must list each Senior/Key person with prefix, names, project role, base salary, calendar/academic/summer months, requested salary, fringe benefits, and funds requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide totals for all Senior/Key Persons and attach supporting files if additional personnel listed; supply accurate months of effort (e.g., 3.0 calendar months = 25% effort) and justify in Budget Justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Personnel budget fields and categories
rubrics_metrics.description: For Other Personnel, provide number of personnel by role, months of effort (calendar/academic/summer), requested salary, fringe benefits, and funds requested; common categories include postdoctoral associates, graduate students, undergraduate students, secretarial/clerical, financial officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize total number of other personnel and include detailed line items in attachments; ensure fringe calculations are shown and consistent with institutional policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment reporting threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: List equipment items and dollar amount for each item exceeding $5,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only items > $5,000 must be listed individually; include total funds requested for all equipment in attached files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel costs — domestic and foreign
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget must separate domestic travel (including Canada, Mexico, U.S. possessions) and foreign travel costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide cost estimates (airfare, per diem, hotel) and justify trips in Budget Justification (e.g., hands-on training at host institution, workshops, visits by U.S. personnel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant/Trainee Support Costs categories
rubrics_metrics.description: If participant/trainee support costs are requested, budget must include tuition/fees/health insurance, stipends, travel, subsistence, and other support items, and number of participants/trainees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide totals and justify amounts per participant; list number of participants and aggregate costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Direct Costs line items
rubrics_metrics.description: Other Direct Costs must be itemized (materials and supplies, publication costs, consultant services, ADP/computer services, subawards/consortium/contractual costs, equipment or facility rental/user fees, alterations and renovations, and other specified items such as translations, development of online components, distance learning/webinars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Itemize and justify unusual or recurring 'Other' costs (e.g., translations to Spanish, development of online training components, grant tracking system) in the Budget Justification and attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect Costs reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify Indirect Cost Type (e.g., MTDC), Cognizant Federal Agency (name, POC, phone), Indirect Cost Rate (%), Indirect Cost Base ($), and Funds Requested for indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide documentation of negotiated indirect cost rates if applicable; calculate total indirect costs and show base and rate used (e.g., 8.0% shown in form).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Justification — personnel effort and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget Justification must describe each Senior/Key and Other Personnel's qualifications, percent effort (calendar months), specific responsibilities on the project, and how their time will be used to meet project objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include biographical/qualification details (degrees, relevant experience), explicit percent effort (e.g., 'will devote 25% effort (3.0 calendar months)'), and clear linkage between duties and project goals (examples provided for PD/PI, co-investigator, financial officer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Justification — travel and activity justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify international and domestic travel (purpose, estimated airfare, per diem, duration, number of travelers) aligned to training and project activities (hands-on training, workshops, visits by host institution personnel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide per diem/day x number of days, airfare estimates, and clearly link travel to training plan phases and deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative budget completeness and totals
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide cumulative totals by budget categories (Sections A–K): total salary/wages and fringe (A+B), equipment (C), travel (D: domestic/foreign), participant support (E), other direct costs (F items 1–10), direct costs (G), indirect costs (H), total direct and indirect (I), fee (J), and total costs and fee (K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show totals in dollars and ensure internal consistency across sections; attach single Budget_justification.pdf as requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims — clarity and measurable objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: The Specific Aims must state the overall goal(s) and enumerate specific objectives with clear activities (e.g., institutionalize grants management best practices; implement continuous training on NIH policies; revise institutional policies/SOPs for NIH compliance; develop and implement ICT tools; adapt and pilot training materials; form interinstitutional community).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims should be concise and include actionable specific objectives that tie directly to measurable implementation steps (training, policy revision, ICT development, dissemination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy — diagnosis of current process and gap analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Strategy should describe the current grants administration/financial management process, identify gaps across pre-award, award, and post-award phases, and provide evidence sources (e.g., FOS visit, internal experience) used to identify gaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include schematic descriptions (figures), flow of information, analysis of causes, and references to existing Quality Management System documents; explicitly list and address identified gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address specific pre-award gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-award phase shortcomings to address include: keeping institutional registrations up to date (Grants.gov, SAMS, eRA Commons) and preparation of budget and institutional research training grant data tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan activities to ensure timely registration updates and to standardize budget/data table preparation procedures and checklists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address specific award-phase gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Award-phase shortcomings to address include collecting Just In Time (JIT) information and reviewing the Notice of Award with PD/PIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement procedures, checklists, and roles to ensure timely JIT collection and thorough NOA review with Principal Investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address specific post-award gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-award shortcomings to address include effort reporting, subrecipient management and monitoring, prior approvals requests, financial reporting and closeout, and clarity of roles/responsibilities (who/when/how/what/why) for financial and administrative monitoring and supervision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review and revise procedures and tools for these processes, implement monitoring plans for subrecipients, define prior-approval workflows, and document role descriptions and SOPs; include these in training materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalize policies, procedures, and SOPs
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to processes must be formalized via institutional policies, procedures and SOPs, communicated to staff, and incorporated into continuing training activities and materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure documentation specifies how tasks are done (how, who, when, what, why), update job descriptions, and disseminate via institutional communications and training curricula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training plan phases and deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: The training plan must include three phases: (1) training of senior administrators at the U.S. host institution (hands-on training), (2) implementation of internal training at the grantee institution, and (3) training offered to external/local/regional institutions (adaptation and piloting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliverables include development of training materials (trainer guide in Spanish), piloting and iterative adaptation, web-based seminars, and sustainability plans for continuing education; training schedule and PERT chart/SDLC steps should be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and pilot training materials and ICT tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop initial participant and trainer materials (including translated trainer guide), pilot and adapt materials in Spanish, create web-based seminars, develop online components for the training program, and design/develop a new in-house Grant Tracking System to support grant management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for iterative design/development/testing/evaluation (e.g., ADDIE model, SDLC), allocate budget and timeline (Y1–Y2 tasks shown), and include costs for translations, online development, and system development in Other Direct Costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability and regional dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Project must include sustainability initiatives: institutionalization of continuous training and updating per NIH guideline changes, and dissemination/adaptation of training for other institutions in the region to form an interinstitutional community of NIH grant managers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a sustainability plan, strategies to institutionalize practices (job descriptions, SOPs, QMS integration), and mechanisms for regional outreach (pilots, webinars, community formation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring, reporting, and evaluation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Project oversight must include regular meetings (e.g., monthly), site visits by host institution trainers, mid-program progress review (e.g., month 10 visit), and required reporting such as annual RPPR, Final RPPR, invention statements, and final FFR for award closeout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document monitoring schedule, reporting milestones, expected deliverables, and include plans for follow-up, in-situ review, and submission of reports to NIH per instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Quality Management System and documented processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant administration should be managed within an institutional Quality Management System supported by manuals, procedures, and formats that guide proposal development, internal approvals, initiation/monitoring/closeout meetings and forms, and compliance with ethical and scientific standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide or reference the QMS documents; ensure internal evaluation of pre-proposals for alignment and compliance; use initiation and closeout forms and convene required meetings for oversight.
